item.title: Dry weather leaves parts of Taveuni without reliable water for almost a week
item.description: Antornette Vuniuca , Rashika Kumar · 31/07/2026 A resident from Naselesele told fijivillage News the community has had little to no water since last Saturday, raising concerns about the continuing shortage.
item.content:encoded:
Antornette Vuniuca , Rashika Kumar · 31/07/2026

A resident from Naselesele told fijivillage News the community has had little to no water since last Saturday, raising concerns about the continuing shortage.

Responding to questions from fijivillage News, the Water Authority of Fiji says it is aware of the issue and has received a high number of complaints from affected customers.

WAF says the prolonged dry spell has significantly reduced water levels at the Mua raw water source, affecting water production and supply across several communities.

The affected areas include Naselesele Village and Primary School, Valevatu Saioni, Vunikavika, Vunitarawa, New Town, Vatudovia, Vuniweleti, Nagasau, Wiwi Village, Raiwasa Hotel, Taveuni Palm, Maravu Resort, Tight Ridge, Coconut Grove and Matei Point.

WAF says its operations team is carrying out regular valve operations and water rationing to manage the limited supply and ensure water is distributed as fairly as possible among affected communities.

The Authority says normal water supply will only be fully restored once there is sustained rainfall and the island's raw water sources recover.

Questions have also been sent to the National Disaster Risk Management Office on assistance for the people of Taveuni.

item.title: Emotional reunion as six rescued medical officers arrive safely at Lakeba Hospital
item.description: Emotional scenes unfolded as the six medical officers who were missing at sea for more than 30 hours arrived at Lakeba Subdivision Hospital, where they were welcomed by colleagues and loved ones. Many were seen in tears as they embraced one another, bringing an end to an anxious search that had prompted prayers and concern from people across the country.
item.content:encoded:
Emotional scenes unfolded as the six medical officers who were missing at sea for more than 30 hours arrived at Lakeba Subdivision Hospital, where they were welcomed by colleagues and loved ones.

Many were seen in tears as they embraced one another, bringing an end to an anxious search that had prompted prayers and concern from people across the country.

The Ministry of Health says the six are in a stable condition at Lakeba Subdivision Hospital.

The Ministry has confirmed to fijivillage News that all six were brought to the hospital earlier today for medical assessment following their rescue southwest of Lakeba.

They say the medical workers remain under observation and are receiving the necessary care.

The six had been reported missing after the boat they were travelling in experienced engine failure while returning from a medical outreach programme in the Southern Lau Group.

The Republic of Fiji Navy earlier confirmed that all six were rescued safely after they were located southwest of Lakeba by the vessel Lomaiviti Princess 12.

The Health Ministry has thanked everyone involved in the search and rescue operation, as well as those who kept the medical workers in their thoughts and prayers.

item.title: Govt-funded funeral, fire and accident assistance scheme ends tomorrow
item.description: The scheme provided one-off financial assistance to eligible social welfare recipients. The Ministry of Women, Children and Social Protection says the scheme, administered by the Ministry of Finance, will cease from tomorrow following the approval of the 2026–2027 National Budget, under which no funding was allocated for its continuation.
item.content:encoded:
The scheme provided one-off financial assistance to eligible social welfare recipients.

The Ministry of Women, Children and Social Protection says the scheme, administered by the Ministry of Finance, will cease from tomorrow following the approval of the 2026–2027 National Budget, under which no funding was allocated for its continuation.

The Ministry says that while the scheme will end, Government assistance in these areas will continue through existing programmes and relevant Government agencies.

They say the Government has allocated $75,000 in the 2026-2027 financial year for immediate fire relief assistance under the Ministry of Women, Children and Social Protection, while the Ministry of Housing has been allocated $200,000 for fire reconstruction assistance.

They add that assistance for unclaimed bodies and healthcare-related support will also continue through relevant Government agencies, including the Ministry of Health and Medical Services.

The Ministry says the Government has allocated about $184 million in the 2026-2027 financial year to support its key social protection programmes, including the Family Assistance Scheme, Child Protection Allowance, Disability Allowance Scheme, Social Pension Scheme, Transport Assistance Programme and the Allowance for Rural Pregnant Mothers.

They say they will continue to monitor the effectiveness and sustainability of the Government's social protection programmes and may revisit the Insurance Scheme for Social Welfare Recipients in future policy and budget discussions, with the public to be informed of any changes.

item.title: Bula Earth: British Army soldier turns life experiences into purpose-driven brand
item.description: Bula means life, and for British Army soldier Margaret Williams, the meaning behind the word is deeply personal as she ventures into her new clothing brand Bula Earth. As the director of the Bula Earth clothing brand, Williams chose the name based on her own life journey and two decades of experience serving in the medical field as a combat soldier.
item.content:encoded:
Bula means life, and for British Army soldier Margaret Williams, the meaning behind the word is deeply personal as she ventures into her new clothing brand Bula Earth.

As the director of the Bula Earth clothing brand, Williams chose the name based on her own life journey and two decades of experience serving in the medical field as a combat soldier.

While speaking to fijivillage News, Williams says she hopes her brand and vision will inspire other Fijians to pursue their dreams and create meaningful opportunities.

The former Saint Joseph Secondary School student comes from a strong family business background, with both of her parents operating their own business.

Their entrepreneurial spirit motivated Williams to follow a similar path and build a name for herself after completing her military service.

Through Bula Earth, she aims to combine her experiences, values, and passion into a brand that represents purpose, resilience, and inspiration.

She says she wants her brand to become a recognized lifestyle brand that reaches people from around the world.

Williams says the biggest challenge has been balancing everything from working in healthcare, serving in the military, and also raising a family and building this business.

She says her unique, stylish, and comfortable quality fabric is what makes her Bula Earth special, which is sourced for su perior tropical comfort and long lasting quality.

Williams stresses that her brand is about positivity, gratitude, culture and living life fully and can be bought online on bulaearth.store.

item.title: Ra women's group turns farming training into thriving nursery business
item.description: Women from Navolau No. 1 Village in Ra are turning agricultural training into a sustainable business after becoming an approved supplier of vegetable and fruit seedlings to the Ministry of Agriculture, Waterways and Sugar Industry, following training in Sustainable Land Management and Farm Management. The Marama ni Navutalakise Cluster, which is part of the Yavusa Burenitu, recently completed the
item.content:encoded:
Women from Navolau No. 1 Village in Ra are turning agricultural training into a sustainable business after becoming an approved supplier of vegetable and fruit seedlings to the Ministry of Agriculture, Waterways and Sugar Industry, following training in Sustainable Land Management and Farm Management.

The Marama ni Navutalakise Cluster, which is part of the Yavusa Burenitu, recently completed the training facilitated by the Ministry, gaining practical skills in nursery management, seedling production and sustainable farming practices.

The training has already produced results, with the women's group now recognised as an approved vendor to supply vegetable and fruit seedlings to the Ministry in Ra Province.

The achievement provides the cluster with a sustainable source of income while supporting the Ministry's efforts to improve farmers' access to quality planting materials across the province.

To help meet the growing demand for seedlings and maintain the required quality standards, the cluster worked closely with Ministry officials to establish a nursery.

The new nursery will allow the group to increase seedling production, improve efficiency and ensure a reliable supply of healthy, high-quality vegetable and fruit seedlings.

It is also expected to strengthen the long-term sustainability of the business while creating more economic opportunities for the women involved.

Cluster President Alena Beraua says the Sustainable Land Management and Farm Management training has given members the knowledge and confidence to improve their farming activities and pursue new income-generating opportunities.

Beraua says becoming a recognised supplier to the Ministry is a proud achievement that reflects the dedication and hard work of the group's members.

She says the training has equipped them with the skills to produce quality seedlings and manage their nursery more effectively, adding that they are committed to maintaining the standards expected by the Ministry.

Beraua says the establishment of the nursery has given the women the confidence to expand their operations and meet the increasing demand for quality planting materials.

She says the group's vision is to grow the nursery into a reliable supplier of quality planting materials while creating more economic opportunities for women in the cluster.

Beraua adds they hope their success will inspire other women's groups to embrace agriculture as a pathway to sustainable livelihoods, while benefiting farming communities throughout Ra Province.

The Ministry of Agriculture, Waterways and Sugar Industry says it will continue supporting community-based groups through training and capacity-building programmes that empower women, promote climate-smart agriculture and create sustainable livelihood opportunities.
